classification.difficultyReason: Inspect each system to choose substitution for an isolated variable or elimination with suitable multipliers, then carry out the linked solving steps; method selection is required but no unsignposted reframing is needed.

content.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations. Use the most appropriate method.

answer.worked:
Elimination: multiply the second equation by 3 and add.
$$\begin{align*}9x-3y&=3\\(2x+3y)+(9x-3y)&=8+3\\11x&=11\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}3(1)-y&=1\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Check: $2(1)+3(2)=8$ and $3(1)-2=1$.

Elimination: multiply the first equation by 2 and the second by 3, then subtract.
$$\begin{align*}4x-6y&=8\\9x-6y&=33\\(9x-6y)-(4x-6y)&=33-8\\5x&=25\\x&=5\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation.
$$\begin{align*}2(5)-3y&=4\\3y&=6\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Check: $2(5)-3(2)=4$ and $3(5)-2(2)=11$.

Substitute $y=5-2x$ into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}2x-3(5-2x)&=17\\2x-15+6x&=17\\8x-15&=17\\8x&=32\\x&=4\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}y&=5-2(4)\\y&=-3\end{align*}$$
Check: $-3=5-2(4)$ and $2(4)-3(-3)=17$.

Substitute $y=2x+8$ into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}2x+8&=-3x-2\\5x&=-10\\x&=-2\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(-2)+8\\y&=4\end{align*}$$
Check: $4=2(-2)+8$ and $4=-3(-2)-2$.

Substitute $x=1-3y$ into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}3y-2(1-3y)&=4\\3y-2+6y&=4\\9y-2&=4\\9y&=6\\y&=\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}x&=1-3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\\x&=-1\end{align*}$$
Check: $-1=1-3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)$ and $3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)-2(-1)=4$.

Substitute $x=2y+1$ into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}2y+1&=3y-2\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}x&=2(3)+1\\x&=7\end{align*}$$
Check: $7=2(3)+1$ and $7=3(3)-2$.

Elimination: multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 2, then subtract.
$$\begin{align*}6x-12y&=39\\6x-10y&=34\\(6x-10y)-(6x-12y)&=34-39\\2y&=-5\\y&=-\frac{5}{2}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation.
$$\begin{align*}2x-4\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right)&=13\\2x+10&=13\\2x&=3\\x&=\frac{3}{2}\end{align*}$$
Check: $2\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)-4\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right)=13$ and $3\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)-5\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right)=17$.

Elimination: multiply the second equation by 2 and subtract the first equation.
$$\begin{align*}4x+8y&=6\\(4x+8y)-(4x+5y)&=6-4\\3y&=2\\y&=\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}2x+4\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)&=3\\2x&=\frac{1}{3}\\x&=\frac{1}{6}\end{align*}$$
Check: $4\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+5\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)=4$ and $2\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+4\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)=3$.

Substitute $y=5-9x$ into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}5x-3(5-9x)&=1\\5x-15+27x&=1\\32x-15&=1\\32x&=16\\x&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}y&=5-9\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\y&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$
Check: $\frac{1}{2}=5-9\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ and $5\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-3\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=1$.

Substitute $y=4x-2$ into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}4x-2&=6x-\frac{7}{2}\\\frac{3}{2}&=2x\\x&=\frac{3}{4}\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}y&=4\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)-2\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
Check: $1=4\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)-2$ and $1=6\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)-\frac{7}{2}$.

Substitute $x=3y+3$ into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}3y+3&=6y+1\\3y&=2\\y&=\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}x&=3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+3\\x&=5\end{align*}$$
Check: $5=3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+3$ and $5=6\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+1$.

Substitute $x=1-y$ into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}7(1-y)-y&=2\\7-7y-y&=2\\7-8y&=2\\8y&=5\\y&=\frac{5}{8}\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}x&=1-\frac{5}{8}\\x&=\frac{3}{8}\end{align*}$$
Check: $\frac{3}{8}=1-\frac{5}{8}$ and $7\left(\frac{3}{8}\right)-\frac{5}{8}=2$.
